_comment: Templates that switch a page to each layout the package ships besides the default one, for developers and CI. A Proclaim template is its params blob, so each entry is a copy of the installed Default template's params with `params` merged over it (values as strings, the way the form saves them). A template is applied through a menu item, not a `t=` query parameter, which is ignored once a menu item matches; so each `pages` entry becomes a menu item (note `<marker>templates`) whose page build/verify-frontend.php fetches as a guest. `expect` is markup only that layout produces; `differsFromDefault` (default true) also asserts the same view under the Default template does not contain it. That cannot hold for `sermonstemplate = simple` while the site is in Simple Mode, which a fresh install is: Default renders the same layout then. `item` names a row from content.json (`teacher:<key>` or `series:<key>`) for views that show one. `undeclared` lists params no form declares, which a site can only have from old data or an import; every other key must be declared in admin/forms/template.xml, because the form drops undeclared keys on save. Only `sermonstemplate` is selectable from the admin on a fresh install; the teacher and series layouts are not (see the issue tracker: teacher cards/list unselectable, useexpert_* undeclared). The series-list custom layout is left out until its 500 is fixed; add it then.
